content_of_post_to_comment: Unpopular opinion: City and transportation planning only needs about 10% of the public meetings it currently holds. Asking an entire neighborhood their opinion about how tall a building should be or if a speed bump should be installed does more harm than good. The Hyper-Public-Meeting-Era of planning was an understandable response to urban renewal demolitions and Robert Moses style highway building, but it's been taken way too far and needs to stop.
comment: The tricky line may be less about fewer meetings and more about better representation: public input is most valuable when it reveals lived impacts, not when it becomes a veto over technical tradeoffs.
